# External datasets

Why the benchmark does not simply reuse a public spreadsheet benchmark, and how each candidate is (or is not) used. Checked 2026-10-09.

The benchmark needs: real workbooks (values **and** formulas), questions whose gold answers come from the workbook rather than from a model, and enough size and mess to stress an encoding. Our own 14 workbooks meet the second need but were built alongside the format, so a result on them alone invites the objection that the test was designed for Sheetmark.

## Candidates

| Dataset | What it is | Why not usable as it is | Use here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [SpreadsheetBench](https://spreadsheetbench.github.io/) ([data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/KAKA22/SpreadsheetBench), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14991)), CC BY-SA 4.0 | 912 tasks (400 "verified") from Excel forum questions; each has an `init` workbook, an instruction, an `answer_position` and a `golden` workbook | 1. **Manipulation, not reading.** Tasks say "write a formula / fill these cells", scored by comparing the produced workbook with the golden one. Our runner is one-shot QA over an encoded workbook, so a task has to be restated as "what values end up in these cells". That tests reasoning about the instruction as much as reading the encoding. 2. **Mostly small.** In the verified set the median cell-level workbook has 71 non-empty cells (90th percentile 703); only 43 of 275 have 300 or more. 3. **Data issues:** 5 tasks lack files, 18 `init` workbooks have formulas with no cached values (an encoding needs values), 2 have multi-range answers, 1 names a missing sheet. 4. **Licence:** share-alike, so the workbooks and anything derived from them are not committed here; a script downloads a pinned revision instead. | Adapted subset: cell-level tasks above a size threshold, restated as value questions on the answer cells, scored against the golden values. Questions are written by third parties, which answers the "designed for the format" objection. |
| [MiMoTable](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.173/) | 1,719 QA triplets over 428 real Excel files | Questions were generated by GPT-4o, so the "gold" answers are model-written; some answers are files or charts rather than values; the GitHub repo returned 403 from this environment. | Not used. |
| Enron spreadsheet corpus ([paper](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/304552688_Enron's_Spreadsheets_and_Related_Emails_A_Dataset_and_Analysis)) | 15,000+ real corporate workbooks, about half with formulas | No questions or answers. The files are in figshare article 1221767 (`spreadsheets.7z`, 15,929 files, CC BY 4.0). | Used in the benchmark set `realworld2/`: 15 formula-heavy workbooks, one per author, picked and questioned by the rules in `realworld2.py`. |
| [FUSE](https://jssmith1.github.io/assets/pdf/MSR15_FUSE.pdf) | 249,376 unique spreadsheets from a web crawl | No questions or answers; mostly raw data dumps. | Not used. |

## Real-world set (built)

`realworld/` holds 17 public workbooks and 67 questions (docs/PROTOCOL.md section 3; experiment E24). Unlike SpreadsheetBench it needs no restating: the questions are about reading the workbook (lookup, address, trace, impact). Twelve source files are open-licence and already in `tests/real/`; the four Damodaran models have no explicit licence and are fetched by hash. The questions and answers are our own facts about those files, so they are committed.

## Rules for any external set

- Pin the source revision and record it with the results.
- Select tasks by a rule written down before any model run (size threshold, task type), never by looking at model results.
- Ground truth comes from the source's own answer files or from recalculation, never typed by hand.
- Keep it separate from the 14-workbook corpus so old results stay comparable.

## Benchmark real-world set (built)

`realworld2/` holds 30 workbooks (15 Damodaran, 15 Enron) for the benchmark run (docs/PROTOCOL.md section 3). Unlike `realworld/`, nothing in it is hand-picked: `realworld2.py select` screens the source files and draws the workbooks with a fixed seed, and `realworld2.py build` draws six questions per workbook by type, computes their answers and leaves out the questions on its exclusion list (163 questions). `selection.json` records every file screened and why it was or was not eligible. The 15 Damodaran files are not redistributed: `realworld2.py fetch` downloads each `.xls`, checks it against `source_sha256`, converts it with LibreOffice and checks the result against `cell_sha256` (the workbook's content; a conversion never repeats its bytes, so the freeze lists these by content). `questions.md` lists every question with its answer and what it was built from. `benchmarks/freeze.py` writes `benchmarks/freeze/benchmark.json`, whose digest is posted publicly before the run.
